display.purpose: Hero headlines only. Tight compression is the brand voice — do not relax line-height.

headline.purpose: Section headings. Same compression as Display, scaled to section hierarchy.

title.purpose: Card headings, service titles, named list items.

body.purpose: All paragraph copy. Max 520–640px container width.

label.purpose: Eyebrows, KPIs, code annotations, form field labels, system metadata. Always JetBrains Mono.

shadows.name: hover-lift
shadows.purpose: Interactive card hover state. Encodes interactivity, not rest-state decoration.

shadows.name: system-widget
shadows.purpose: Terminal and code editor panels. Grounds dark widgets against lighter backgrounds.

shadows.name: active-glow
shadows.purpose: Pipeline node active state in the live demo animation only. Never on static elements.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Form input focus. Orange signal color, 4px soft ring.

motion.name: ease-reveal
motion.purpose: Scroll reveal transitions (opacity + translateY). Default easing for section entrances.

motion.name: ease-state
motion.purpose: State transitions: button hover, card hover, border-color changes. Short duration (0.15–0.25s).

motion.name: reveal-duration
motion.purpose: Scroll reveal opacity + transform transition duration.

motion.name: stagger-step
motion.purpose: Stagger delay increment between sibling elements in reveal-stagger groups.

breakpoints.name: mobile
breakpoints.purpose: Single-column stacking for tight grids (stack, process).

breakpoints.name: tablet
breakpoints.purpose: Section padding reduction, body text adjustments.

breakpoints.name: desktop-sm
breakpoints.purpose: Nav links hidden, hero/contact/about grids collapse to single column.

narrative.overview:
Every margin is load-bearing. Every color earns its place. The Agencia Byte design system does not decorate — it specifies. Like reading a well-written API spec that happens to be beautiful: no superfluous words, no flourish for its own sake, every element doing exactly its assigned job.

The visual language is built on three structural moves: tight display typography (-0.02em tracking, 0.98 line-height) that reads as engineered rather than styled; a strict orange signal that activates only on live, interactive, or actionable states — never decorative; and a light/dark section alternation that creates structural rhythm without requiring graphical complexity. The dark sections are not mood boards. They are command surfaces.

This system explicitly rejects: SaaS genérico patterns (purple gradients, hero metric grids), cheap outsourcing aesthetics (stock photography, generic icons), and creative agency maximalism (image-led layouts). Agencia Byte builds systems — the demos, terminals, and pipeline animations are the visual content.
keyCharacteristics: Tight typographic control — display headings near line-height 1, heavy negative tracking
Structural dark/light alternation as the primary depth strategy
Mono type as a technical annotation layer, not decoration
Orange reserved for live signals and primary actions only
Gridded backdrops as ambient texture, never focal points
Interaction feedback through translateY lift, not color flood

rules.name: The Rarity Rule
rules.body: Live Signal Orange covers at most 10–15% of any given screen. One CTA, one status dot, one active node — that is its full budget. A screen where orange appears on a card icon, a list bullet, a badge, a headline, AND a button has broken the rule.

rules.name: The No-Pure-Black Rule
rules.body: Neither #000000 nor #FFFFFF appear in this system. Every neutral is tinted toward the deep navy hue family. Pure white or black reads as system default; the tinted versions read as designed.

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Orange marks only live, active, or actionable states. It is never used as a decorative accent, background pattern, or divider color. If it appears, it must mean something.

rules.name: The Mono Thread Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is the annotation layer. It appears at eyebrow scale (11–13px), never at headline scale. If you reach for Mono to headline something, you are using the wrong font — Space Grotesk at 700 is the headline voice.

rules.name: The Compression Rule
rules.body: Display and Headline typography uses 0.98 and 1.05 line-heights respectively. Do not round up to 1.2 for readability. The compression is the statement.

rules.name: The Flat-at-Rest Rule
rules.body: No card, panel, or container has a box-shadow at rest. Shadows encode state (hover, active, elevated widget). A static shadow is a decoration; this system does not decorate.

dos: Do use Live Signal Orange only on CTAs, active pipeline nodes, animated status indicators, and the eyebrow dot.
Do set display headlines with letter-spacing: -0.02em and line-height: 0.98.
Do use JetBrains Mono for all system metadata: version numbers, code comments, metric units, form field labels, eyebrow text.
Do alternate light and dark sections as the primary depth and rhythm mechanism.
Do add prefers-reduced-motion media queries to all animations.
Do ensure all text meets WCAG AAA contrast: 7:1 for normal text, 4.5:1 for large text.
Do place focus-visible outlines on all interactive elements using the orange accent at 2px, 3px offset.
donts: Don't use purple gradients, hero metric grids, or copy patterns like '10x your growth' — SaaS genérico is the primary anti-reference.
Don't use stock photography or image-heavy layouts.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text with a gradient fill).
Don't use border-left greater than 1px as a colored stripe on cards, callouts, or list items.
Don't apply glassmorphism beyond the nav blur.
Don't add identical card grids with icon + heading + text repeated without variation.
Don't use orange as a background color on large surfaces.
Don't create walls of dense text with no typographic hierarchy.
